final_candidates.decision_summary: R157 lies in the highly conserved catalytic motif (RLEEITGH); a proline substitution would disrupt backbone geometry and local structure, very likely abolishing catalytic activity.
Introducing a bulky charged aspartate at a conserved glycine adjacent to the active-site motif should sterically and electrostatically disrupt the catalytic pocket.
A222 is the known functionally sensitive C677T locus; a proline here is far more destabilizing than the natural Val variant and should collapse catalytic-domain folding and activity.

stop_reason.detail: Self-review converged; no external evidence is available to further refine rankings.

history.rationale: Arg157 lies in the highly conserved N-terminal catalytic (FAD-dependent reductase) domain; R157 substitutions are known severe MTHFR-deficiency alleles. Proline at this position should disrupt local structure and abolish catalysis.
R157 lies in a highly conserved catalytic-domain motif (RLEEITGH); proline substitution would disrupt local helix/backbone and likely abolish catalysis. Retain as top candidate.
Gly158 is adjacent to the catalytic Arg157 in a conserved segment; introducing a bulky charged Asp should distort the active-site region and eliminate activity.
G158D introduces a bulky charged residue into a conserved loop adjacent to the active site; strong candidate for abolishing activity.
Ala222 is the site of the classic thermolabile A222V (C677T) polymorphism; the more drastic A222P substitution should more completely destabilize the catalytic domain and abolish function.
A222 (the C677T/Ala222Val locus) is known to be functionally sensitive; a proline here is far more disruptive than the natural Val variant and should destabilize the catalytic domain.
Trp165 sits in a conserved stretch of the catalytic domain near the presumed FAD/substrate binding region; removing the large aromatic side chain should impair cofactor binding or catalysis.
W165A removes a large aromatic side chain in the active-site region, likely destabilizing local packing and cofactor binding. Keep but rank just below charge-disrupting mutations.
Glu166 is part of a conserved acidic patch in the catalytic domain that may participate in substrate/cofactor interactions; alanine substitution could abolish activity.

E166 sits in the conserved catalytic cleft near the glycine-rich loop; removing a charged residue here likely impairs FAD/substrate handling. Rerank up slightly over W165A since point charge loss is more reliably disruptive than Trp truncation uncertainty.
Gly171 begins the conserved GFNYA motif in the catalytic domain; a charged Asp at this small-residue position should disrupt fold or active-site geometry.
G171 is in the glycine-rich segment; introducing a bulky acidic residue should sterically block the catalytic pocket.
Asp163 is a conserved acidic residue in the catalytic core; conservative neutralization may impair charge-dependent steps in catalysis.
Asp-to-Asn is conservative and often tolerated; unlikely to fully abolish activity. Reject to focus on more disruptive changes.

rejection.reason: Asp-to-Asn is conservative and often tolerated; unlikely to fully abolish activity. Reject to focus on more disruptive changes.

history.rationale: Cys243 is a conserved cysteine in the catalytic domain; serine/alanine substitutions at cysteines in this region can disrupt redox chemistry or structural integrity.
C243 is less clearly catalytic and Cys-to-Ala is frequently tolerated; lower confidence for complete loss of function.

rejection.reason: C243 is less clearly catalytic and Cys-to-Ala is frequently tolerated; lower confidence for complete loss of function.
